subject: Dedicated capacity: traffic handoff + sizing clarifications (DataBridge)
messages:
From: Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@databridgelabs.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@databridgelabs.com>, sales@databridgelabs.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity handoff + initial traffic export

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — super helpful. As discussed, attaching a small extract of our production traffic so you can validate the sizing assumptions. A few quick clarifications we need answered before the internal procurement review: 

- We expect steady-state requests of ~220 RPS for the multi-tenant inference endpoint, with 95th-percentile bursts up to 450 RPS for short windows (1-2 minutes). Is that pattern reasonable for Redwood Dedicated?
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens. Typical generated response: 320 tokens. We also have a handful of endpoints that use streaming for partial responses. Any specific recommendations for model variants for lower-latency streaming?
- We use session pinning for a subset of users (approx 18% of traffic) where KV cache reuse is expected. How should we represent cache-hit assumptions in sizing?

I've attached db-traffic-sample-20270420.csv (10k row sample) and included a high-level SLA target: P99 latency for first token <= 750ms on standard routes.

Can you confirm what additional fields you need in the extract (e.g., per-request seq length, auth tier, region)? We can produce an expanded dump if that helps your estimate.

Thanks,
Aisha
DataBridge Labs

Attachments: db-traffic-sample-20270420.csv (CSV, 1.1 MB)

From: olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>
To: Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@databridgelabs.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, dev.patel@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity handoff + initial traffic export

Hi Aisha — thanks for the sample and the notes. Quick read-through and a few asks so we can run a deterministic capacity model: 

1) Concurrency profile: can you provide approximate distribution across the day (off-peak, peak 95th, and burst windows)? A short CSV with timestamped RPS or a percentile table is perfect.
2) Token distribution: do you have median/95th token counts for prompt and response separately? The sample looked skewed; we need those percentiles to pick batch/kv tradeoffs.
3) Streaming endpoints: for streaming first-token latency we commonly recommend a lower-headroom model (e.g., distilled or lower-parameter variant) and aggressive batching thresholds per route — happy to propose specific model candidates after we see the P95/P99 sequence lengths.
4) KV cache reuse: if 18% of traffic reuses session-state, do you have per-session average sequence length? Cache hit rate assumptions materially change GPU memory and KV-shard placement.

Internal next steps: Vivek and Marissa — I'll loop you in on the CSV and would like a quick estimation of GPU SKUs (A100 vs H100 vs L4 equivalent) and a mapping to committed slots for DBL's usage profile. Dev — can you prepare the dedicated sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) for Aisha to fill the percentile tables?

Aisha — if helpful, we can run an initial sizing using the sample and return a deterministic quorum (number of GPUs, suggested SKUs, expected p99 token latency vs model variant) by EOD tomorrow. Let me know if that timeline works.

Best,
Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (XLSX, 84 KB)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, dev.patel@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:46:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity handoff + initial traffic export

Olga — first pass thoughts (internal):

- Given 220 steady RPS / 450 burst and average combined tokens ~440, we should model both a latency-optimized and cost-optimized fleet.
- Latency plan: H100-prod class (stateful KV-friendly topology) with ~12-16 GPUs mapped to the primary route using continuous batching tuned to keep p99 first-token under 700ms. This assumes ~18% KV reuse with 60-70% hit rate for pinned sessions.
- Cost plan: mixed fleet with quantized variants (int8/4-bit) on L4-like instances for non-pinned traffic. That reduces required H100s to ~6-8 for the heavy hitting routes.
- Important kicker: streaming routes often require smaller model variants (7B-13B) with tight batching windows; recommend a canary with 13B quantized first.

Action items: Marissa — can you run a micro-benchmark matrix on our perf lab (13B quantized streaming vs 70B int8 non-stream) and capture tokens/sec, kv-memory per session, and p99 first-token for 10, 50, 95 concurrency points? Vivek suggests we should instrument an autoscale headroom of 1.8x on burst windows.

Vivek

From: Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@databridgelabs.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@databridgelabs.com>, sales@databridgelabs.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity handoff + initial traffic export

Thanks, Olga — attaching the percentile table you asked for and a fuller dump of session metadata. The attached CSV includes per-request prompt_tokens, response_tokens, user_tier, and session_id. We confirm the 18% session pinning number and estimate a cache-hit around 65% for pinned traffic. We also included a 30-day rolling peak window to show diurnal variation.

Tom (SRE) added a note: if we move to an A100-based cluster for cost reasons, what's the typical impact on p99-first-token compared to H100? We're trying to understand where the break-even sits for our procurement committee.

Aisha

Attachments: db-traffic-sample-20270421-expanded.csv (3.9 MB)

From: olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com <olga.petrov@redwood-inference.com>
To: Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@databridgelabs.com>, Tom Lin <tom.lin@databridgelabs.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, dev.patel@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity handoff + initial traffic export

Aisha / Tom — thanks for the expanded dump, that's exactly what we needed. Summary of the deliverable we're returning to you: 

- Initial deterministic sizing (attached summary): 10 H100-equivalent GPUs for latency-primary fleet to meet P99-first-token <= 750ms with 18% pinned sessions and 65% KV hit; OR a mixed plan with 6 H100 + 8 L4-equivalent quantized workers for cost-optimized ops.
- Recommended model split: 13B-quantized for streaming endpoints; 70B-int8 for non-stream heavy-lift routes.
- Autoscale policy: baseline steady capacity for 220 RPS, autoscale to 1.8x for short bursts (policy windows of 120s), and a separate pool for pinned sessions to avoid cross-tenant eviction.
- Next steps: we will produce a formal Mutual Action Plan and an updated SOW that includes committed GPU slots and canary timelines. Expect a draft M.A.P. by EOD Monday.

Tom — re: A100 vs H100: in our lab benchmarks H100 shows ~25-40% better throughput for the larger 70B variants and better kernel fusion for KV ops; for the 13B streaming workloads the gap narrows and A100 can be a reasonable cost tradeoff if you're comfortable with slightly higher p99 (we'll include a delta table in the MAP).

Olga
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Internal note: Vivek / Marissa / Dev — please assemble benchmark artifacts and put the MAP draft into the HubSpot deal record. Marissa, call with procurement scheduled Tue 2027-04-27 10:00am PT.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf (report, 210 KB)
